claim: Treatment of MLL-fusion leukaemia cells (MV4;11 cell line) with the BET bromodomain inhibitor I-BET151 resulted in selective growth inhibition.
source: We found treatment of MLL-fusion leukaemia cells (MV4;11 cell line) with the BET bromodomain inhibitor I-BET151 resulted in selective growth inhibition, whereas treatment of leukaemia cells harboring a different oncogenic driver (K-562 cell line) did not result in selective growth inhibition; this is similar to the findings reported in the original study (Figure 2A and Supplementary Figure 11A,B; Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing IC50 values and dose-response curves for MV4;11 cells treated with I-BET151, and comparison to original study results.

claim: Treatment of leukaemia cells harboring a different oncogenic driver (K-562 cell line) with I-BET151 did not result in selective growth inhibition.
source: We found treatment of MLL-fusion leukaemia cells (MV4;11 cell line) with the BET bromodomain inhibitor I-BET151 resulted in selective growth inhibition, whereas treatment of leukaemia cells harboring a different oncogenic driver (K-562 cell line) did not result in selective growth inhibition; this is similar to the findings reported in the original study (Figure 2A and Supplementary Figure 11A,B; Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing inability to accurately determine IC50 values for K-562 cells, indicating lack of selective growth inhibition.

claim: I-BET151 resulted in a statistically significant decrease in BCL2 expression in MV4;11 cells.
source: Further, I-BET151 resulted in a statistically significant decrease in BCL2 expression in MV4;11 cells, but not in K-562 cells; again this is similar to the findings reported in the original study (Figure 3D; Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data showing 0.501 mean fold change in BCL2 expression in MV4;11 cells treated with I-BET151, with statistical significance reported.

claim: I-BET151 did not result in a statistically significant decrease in BCL2 expression in K-562 cells.
source: Further, I-BET151 resulted in a statistically significant decrease in BCL2 expression in MV4;11 cells, but not in K-562 cells; again this is similar to the findings reported in the original study (Figure 3D; Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data showing K-562 cells remained largely unchanged with mean fold change of 1.06 in BCL2 expression.

claim: There was no statistically significant difference in survival when testing I-BET151 efficacy in a disseminated xenograft MLL mouse model.
source: We did not find a statistically significant difference in survival when testing I-BET151 efficacy in a disseminated xenograft MLL mouse model, whereas the original study reported increased survival in I-BET151 treated mice compared to vehicle control (Figure 4B,D; Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by survival data showing median survival of 19.0 days for vehicle control and 18.5 days for I-BET151 treated mice, with log-rank test p=0.536.

claim: I-BET151 treatment resulted in a lower median disease burden compared to vehicle control in all tissues analyzed.
source: We also found I-BET151 treatment resulted in a lower median disease burden compared to vehicle control in all tissues analyzed, similar to the example reported in the original study (Supplementary Figure 16A; Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data showing lower median disease burden in peripheral blood, bone marrow, and spleen of I-BET151 treated mice.

claim: The mean absolute IC50 value for I-BET151 treated MV4;11 cells was 9.03 nM.
source: For each cell line, cellular IC50 values were determined (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2) with a mean absolute IC50 value of 9.03 nM [n = 5, SD = 8.27 nM] for I-BET151 treated MV4;11 cells, while the K-562 IC50 estimates were not able to be accurately determined following published guidelines (Sebaugh, 2011).
evidence: Supported by experimental measurements from five biological repeats with calculated IC50 values.

claim: The K-562 IC50 estimates were not able to be accurately determined following published guidelines.
source: For each cell line, cellular IC50 values were determined (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2) with a mean absolute IC50 value of 9.03 nM [n = 5, SD = 8.27 nM] for I-BET151 treated MV4;11 cells, while the K-562 IC50 estimates were not able to be accurately determined following published guidelines (Sebaugh, 2011).
evidence: Supported by experimental data and reference to published guidelines for IC50 determination.

claim: The original study by Dawson et al. reported an IC50 value of 26 nM for MV4;11 cells.
source: This compares to the original study that reported an IC50 value of 26 nM for MV4;11 cells, with the K-562 IC50 value also unable to be accurately determined (Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to the original study by Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: Treatment of MV4;11 cells with I-BET151 resulted in a 0.501 mean fold change in BCL2 expression relative to vehicle control.
source: Using the 2-∆∆Ct method, treatment of MV4;11 cells with I-BET151 resulted in a 0.501 [n = 3, SD = 0.048] mean fold change in BCL2 expression relative to vehicle control, while K-562 cells remained largely unchanged [n = 3, M = 1.06, SD = 0.028].
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR experimental data using the 2-∆∆Ct method from three biological repeats.

claim: K-562 cells remained largely unchanged with a mean fold change of 1.06 in BCL2 expression after I-BET151 treatment.
source: Using the 2-∆∆Ct method, treatment of MV4;11 cells with I-BET151 resulted in a 0.501 [n = 3, SD = 0.048] mean fold change in BCL2 expression relative to vehicle control, while K-562 cells remained largely unchanged [n = 3, M = 1.06, SD = 0.028].
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR experimental data from three biological repeats.

claim: Dawson et al. reported an ~0.22 mean fold change in BCL2 expression for MV4;11 cells.
source: This is similar to Dawson et al. (2011), which reported an ~0.22 mean fold change in BCL2 expression for MV4;11 cells and an ~0.94 mean fold change for the K-562 cell line.
evidence: Supported by citation to the original study by Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: Dawson et al. reported an ~0.94 mean fold change in BCL2 expression for the K-562 cell line.
source: This is similar to Dawson et al. (2011), which reported an ~0.22 mean fold change in BCL2 expression for MV4;11 cells and an ~0.94 mean fold change for the K-562 cell line.
evidence: Supported by citation to the original study by Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: The two-sample t-test comparing fold gene expression values from K-562 cells to MV4;11 cells was statistically significant (t(4) = 17.23, uncorrected p=6.66×10−5, corrected p=0.0004).
source: We performed an unpaired, two-sample t-test on the fold gene expression values from K-562 cells compared to MV4;11 cells, which was statistically significant (t(4) = 17.23, uncorrected p=6.66×10−5, corrected p=0.0004).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental qRT-PCR data.

claim: The one-sample t-test on fold gene expression values from K-562 cells compared to a constant of 1 was not statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (t(2) = 3.53, uncorrected p=0.072, corrected p=0.216).
source: Additionally, we performed a one-sample t-test on the fold gene expression values from K-562 cells compared to a constant of 1 (t(2) = 3.53, uncorrected p=0.072, corrected p=0.216), and a one-sample t-test on the fold gene expression values from MV4;11 cells compared to a constant of 1 (t(2) = 17.86, uncorrected p=0.003, corrected p=0.009).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental qRT-PCR data.

claim: The one-sample t-test on fold gene expression values from MV4;11 cells compared to a constant of 1 was statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (t(2) = 17.86, uncorrected p=0.003, corrected p=0.009).
source: Additionally, we performed a one-sample t-test on the fold gene expression values from K-562 cells compared to a constant of 1 (t(2) = 3.53, uncorrected p=0.072, corrected p=0.216), and a one-sample t-test on the fold gene expression values from MV4;11 cells compared to a constant of 1 (t(2) = 17.86, uncorrected p=0.003, corrected p=0.009).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental qRT-PCR data.

claim: The maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of I-BET151 in the xenograft mouse model was determined as 20 mg/kg/day.
source: Mice were randomized into treatment groups and after 21 days of daily intraperitoneal (IP) injections of vehicle control or three different doses of I-BET151, the MTD was determined as 20 mg/kg/day (Figure 3) based on the criteria pre-specified in the Registered Report (Fung et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from MTD study with multiple dose groups and pre-specified criteria.

claim: The original study delivered I-BET151 daily at 30 mg/kg.
source: For comparison the original study delivered I-BET151 daily at 30 mg/kg.
evidence: Supported by reference to the original study's methods.

claim: Mice treated with vehicle control achieved a median survival of 19.0 days after the start of treatment.
source: After the start of treatment, mice treated with vehicle control achieved a median survival of 19.0 days [n = 11], which is indistinguishable from the 18.5 days [n = 12] observed in mice treated with I-BET151 (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by survival data from the efficacy study.

claim: Mice treated with I-BET151 achieved a median survival of 18.5 days after the start of treatment.
source: After the start of treatment, mice treated with vehicle control achieved a median survival of 19.0 days [n = 11], which is indistinguishable from the 18.5 days [n = 12] observed in mice treated with I-BET151 (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by survival data from the efficacy study.

claim: A log-rank (Mantel-Cox) test comparing survival distributions between vehicle control and I-BET151 treated mice was not statistically significant (p=0.536).
source: A planned comparison between these survival distributions using a log-rank (Mantel-Cox) test was not statistically significant (p=0.536).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of survival data.

claim: The original study reported a median survival of 14 days for vehicle control treated animals.
source: This compares to the original study that reported a median survival of 14 days, [n = 5] for vehicle control treated animals that was lengthened to the experimental end-point of 21 days with I-BET151 treatment.
evidence: Supported by citation to the original study by Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: The original study reported that median survival was lengthened to the experimental end-point of 21 days with I-BET151 treatment.
source: This compares to the original study that reported a median survival of 14 days, [n = 5] for vehicle control treated animals that was lengthened to the experimental end-point of 21 days with I-BET151 treatment.
evidence: Supported by citation to the original study by Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: The median percent of leukaemia cells detected in the bone marrow of vehicle control mice was 10.7%.
source: For example, the median percent of leukaemia cells detected in the bone marrow of vehicle control mice was 10.7%, which was reduced to 5.3% in I-BET151 treated mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data from the efficacy study.

claim: The median percent of leukaemia cells detected in the bone marrow was reduced to 5.3% in I-BET151 treated mice.
source: For example, the median percent of leukaemia cells detected in the bone marrow of vehicle control mice was 10.7%, which was reduced to 5.3% in I-BET151 treated mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data from the efficacy study.

claim: Dawson et al. reported 14% leukaemia burden in the bone marrow of the control mouse.
source: This compares to the representative example reported in Supplementary Figure 16A of Dawson et al. (2011), which reported 14% leukaemia burden in the bone marrow of the control mouse and 1.5% in the I-BET151 treated mouse where low-level residual leukaemia was reported after the 21 day treatment.
evidence: Supported by citation to the original study by Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: Dawson et al. reported 1.5% leukaemia burden in the bone marrow of the I-BET151 treated mouse where low-level residual leukaemia was reported after the 21 day treatment.
source: This compares to the representative example reported in Supplementary Figure 16A of Dawson et al. (2011), which reported 14% leukaemia burden in the bone marrow of the control mouse and 1.5% in the I-BET151 treated mouse where low-level residual leukaemia was reported after the 21 day treatment.
evidence: Supported by citation to the original study by Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: There was a minor decrease in both apoptotic and necrotic cells observed in the bone marrow of I-BET151 treated mice compared to vehicle control.
source: Observationally, there was no notable difference in the peripheral blood or spleen, with a minor decrease in both apoptotic (Annexin V+PI-) and necrotic cells (Annexin V+PI+) observed in the bone marrow of I-BET151 treated mice compared to vehicle control (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data assessing cell death markers.

claim: Gastrointestinal bloating was observed in three of the I-BET151 treated mice at the time of sacrifice.
source: These included gastrointestinal bloating in three of the I-BET151 treated mice and solid tumors detected in four of the vehicle control treated mice and two of the I-BET151 treated mice.
evidence: Supported by observational data from the efficacy study.

claim: Solid tumors were detected in four of the vehicle control treated mice at the time of sacrifice.
source: These included gastrointestinal bloating in three of the I-BET151 treated mice and solid tumors detected in four of the vehicle control treated mice and two of the I-BET151 treated mice.
evidence: Supported by observational data from the efficacy study.

claim: Solid tumors were detected in two of the I-BET151 treated mice at the time of sacrifice.
source: These included gastrointestinal bloating in three of the I-BET151 treated mice and solid tumors detected in four of the vehicle control treated mice and two of the I-BET151 treated mice.
evidence: Supported by observational data from the efficacy study.

claim: In all tested tumor samples there was extensive HLA-A,B,C staining, indicating the injected human leukaemia cells spread throughout the mouse outside the hematological tissues.
source: To explore the origin of the observed tumors, sections were stained using a human leukocyte antigen (HLA-A,B,C) antibody (Figure 4—figure supplement 2). In all tested samples there was extensive staining, indicating the injected human leukaemia cells spread throughout the mouse outside the hematological tissues.
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data showing HLA-A,B,C staining in tumor sections.

claim: The original study reported EMD in the majority of the control mice, in contrast to none of the I-BET151 treated mice.
source: Indeed, the original study reported EMD in the majority of the control mice, in contrast to none of the I-BET151 treated mice (Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to the original study by Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: The meta-analysis of fold BCL2 expression in K-562 cells compared to a constant of 1 resulted in d = −0.307, 95% CI [−3.57,2.96], which was not statistically significant (p=0.854).
source: The comparison of K-562 fold gene expression compared to a constant of 1 resulted in d = −2.04, 95% CI [−4.17, 0.13] in this study, whereas d = 1.30, 95% CI [−0.38, 2.88] for the data estimated a priori from Figure 3D in the original study (Dawson et al., 2011). A meta-analysis of these effects resulted in d = −0.307, 95% CI [−3.57,2.96], which was not statistically significant (p=0.854).
evidence: Supported by meta-analysis combining original and replication effect sizes.

claim: The meta-analysis of fold BCL2 expression in MV4;11 cells compared to a constant of 1 resulted in d = 15.13, 95% CI [0.94, 29.32], which was statistically significant (p=0.037).
source: The comparison of MV4;11 fold gene expression compared to a constant of 1, resulted in d = 10.31, 95% CI [1.54, 19.86] in this replication attempt, d = 26.00, 95% CI [4.10, 48.25] for the data estimated from the original study (Dawson et al., 2011) and d = 15.13, 95% CI [0.94, 29.32] for a meta-analysis of the two effects. Both the original and replication results are consistent when considering the direction of the effect, with the point estimate of the replication effect size was within the confidence interval of the original result and vice versa. Further, the random effects meta-analysis resulted in a statistically significant effect (p=0.037).
evidence: Supported by meta-analysis combining original and replication effect sizes.

claim: The meta-analysis comparing fold BCL2 expression in MV4;11 cells to K-562 cells resulted in d = 15.37, 95% CI [5.99, 24.75], which was statistically significant (p=0.001).
source: For the third comparison between MV4;11 and K-562 fold gene expression, this replication attempted resulted in d = 14.07, 95% CI [4.73, 23.59], which compares to d = 17.34, 95% CI [5.90, 29.04] for the data estimated from the original study (Dawson et al., 2011) (Figure 5B). A meta-analysis of these effects resulted in d = 15.37, 95% CI [5.99, 24.75], which was statistically significant (p=0.001).
evidence: Supported by meta-analysis combining original and replication effect sizes.

claim: The meta-analysis of survival comparing I-BET151 to vehicle control resulted in a HR of 3.30, 95% CI [0.49,22.18], which was not statistically significant (p=0.220).
source: The comparison of the overall survival distributions between mice treated with I-BET151 compared to those that were treated with vehicle control resulted in a HR of 1.44, 95% CI [0.45, 4.56] for this replication attempt compared to a HR of 10.32, 95% CI [1.51, 70.63] for the original study (Dawson et al., 2011). A meta-analysis (Figure 5C) of these effects resulted in a HR of 3.30, 95% CI [0.49,22.18], which was not statistically significant (p=0.220).
evidence: Supported by meta-analysis combining original and replication hazard ratios.

claim: The doubling time of MV4;11 cells was calculated to be 48 hr.
source: The doubling time of each cell line was calculated to be 48 hr and 36.2 hr for the MV4;11 and K-562 cell lines, respectively.
evidence: Supported by experimental measurements using MTS cell proliferation assay.

claim: The doubling time of K-562 cells was calculated to be 36.2 hr.
source: The doubling time of each cell line was calculated to be 48 hr and 36.2 hr for the MV4;11 and K-562 cell lines, respectively.
evidence: Supported by experimental measurements using MTS cell proliferation assay.

claim: Engraftment of MV4;11 cells in NOD-SCID mice occurred 5 weeks after intravenous injection.
source: Five weeks after intravenous injection of MV4;11 cells into 7-week-old female NOD-SCID mice, the animals were successfully engrafted as determined by detectable human leukaemia cells in the peripheral blood.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations from the MTD study.

claim: The time to engraftment was increased from the 3 weeks reported in the original study due to lack of detectable leukaemia cells in mice at 3 weeks post-injection during this replication attempt.
source: This was an increase from the 3 weeks reported in the original study, but was necessary due to the lack of detectable leukaemia cells in mice at 3 weeks post-injection during this replication attempt.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations and comparison to the original study.

claim: Recent work from authors of the original study reported I-BET151 administered at 10 mg/kg had no impact on survival in a MLL-AF9 leukaemia mouse model.
source: Indeed, recent work from authors of the original study reported I-BET151 administered at 10 mg/kg had no impact on survival in a MLL-AF9 leukaemia mouse model (Gilan et al., 2016), while I-BET151 administered at 15 mg/kg did provide a survival benefit in a mouse model of NPM1c AML, albeit with a smaller effect size (Dawson et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to a subsequent study by Gilan et al., 2016.

claim: I-BET151 administered at 15 mg/kg did provide a survival benefit in a mouse model of NPM1c AML, albeit with a smaller effect size.
source: Indeed, recent work from authors of the original study reported I-BET151 administered at 10 mg/kg had no impact on survival in a MLL-AF9 leukaemia mouse model (Gilan et al., 2016), while I-BET151 administered at 15 mg/kg did provide a survival benefit in a mouse model of NPM1c AML, albeit with a smaller effect size (Dawson et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to a study by Dawson et al., 2014.

claim: Differences between the original study and this replication attempt, such as different conditioning regimens and I-BET151 doses, are factors that might have influenced the outcome.
source: Differences between the original study and this replication attempt, such as different conditioning regimens and I-BET151 doses, are factors that might have influenced the outcome.
evidence: Based on inference from comparing methodological differences between studies.

claim: Busulfan conditioning could have influenced engraftment kinetics and disease progression in this animal model and potentially impacted the responsiveness of MV4;11 cells to I-BET151 treatment.
source: Additionally, busulfan conditioning could have influenced engraftment kinetics and disease progression in this animal model and potentially impacted the responsiveness of MV4;11 cells to I-BET151 treatment.
evidence: Based on speculation about potential effects of methodological differences.

claim: Health issues not directly related to leukaemia could have impacted mortality observed in some of the animals, particularly those treated with I-BET151.
source: Collectively, these observations raise the possibility that although a survival benefit was not observed with I-BET151 treatment in this replication attempt, despite an overall reduced disease burden, that health issues not directly related to leukaemia could have impacted mortality observed in some of the animals, particularly those treated with I-BET151.
evidence: Based on inference from observational data about animal health issues and tumor presence.

claim: Studies using structurally distinct BET inhibitors, JQ1 and OTX015, have reported these inhibitors to be highly active in various cell lines, mouse models, and primary patient samples of MLL and other types of AML.
source: Studies using structurally distinct BET inhibitors, JQ1 and OTX015, have reported these inhibitors to be highly active in various cell lines, mouse models, and primary patient samples of MLL and other types of AML (Chen et al., 2013; Coudé et al., 2015; Fiskus et al., 2014; Herrmann et al., 2013; Mertz et al., 2011; Zuber et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies.

claim: I-BET151 was reported to be active against AML with mutations involving the nucleophosmin (NPM1) gene (NPM1c AML).
source: Furthermore, I-BET151 was reported to be active against AML with mutations involving the nucleophosmin (NPM1) gene (NPM1c AML) (Dawson et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to a study by Dawson et al., 2014.

claim: Evidence indicating potential acquired resistance to BET inhibitors has been reported.
source: Additionally, evidence indicating potential acquired resistance to BET inhibitors has been reported (Fong et al., 2015; Kumar et al., 2015; Rathert et al., 2015), along with studies which have found that treatment with combinatorial drugs can mitigate acquired resistance (Asangani et al., 2016; Kurimchak et al., 2016; Yao et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies.

claim: Treatment with combinatorial drugs can mitigate acquired resistance to BET inhibitors.
source: Additionally, evidence indicating potential acquired resistance to BET inhibitors has been reported (Fong et al., 2015; Kumar et al., 2015; Rathert et al., 2015), along with studies which have found that treatment with combinatorial drugs can mitigate acquired resistance (Asangani et al., 2016; Kurimchak et al., 2016; Yao et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies.

claim: A recent study reported synergistic effects of combinatorial treatment with a disruptor of telomeric silencing 1-like (DOT1L) inhibitor and I-BET151 in MLL cells and mouse leukaemia models.
source: Furthermore, a recent study reported synergistic effects of combinatorial treatment with a disruptor of telomeric silencing 1-like (DOT1L) inhibitor and I-BET151 in MLL cells and mouse leukaemia models (Gilan et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to a study by Gilan et al., 2016.

claim: BET bromodomain inhibition can impact normal intestinal homeostasis and repair.
source: Studies have also addressed the nonclinical safety of BET inhibition and found that BET bromodomain inhibition can impact normal intestinal homeostasis and repair (Nakagawa et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to a study by Nakagawa et al., 2016.

claim: A phase I trial to determine the recommended dose of BET inhibitor OTX015/MK-8628 reported that although the inhibitor was found to be tolerated, toxic effects such as thrombocytopenia were commonly observed.
source: A phase I trial to determine the recommended dose of BET inhibitor OTX015/MK-8628 reported that although the inhibitor was found to be tolerated, toxic effects such as thrombocytopenia were commonly observed (Amorim et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to a clinical trial study by Amorim et al., 2016.

claim: An additional clinical study testing BET inhibition with OTX015/MK-8628 in four patients with advanced NUT midline carcinoma, with confirmed BRD4-NUT fusions, found early clinical benefits reported for two patients with one achieving post-treatment disease stabilization.
source: An additional clinical study testing BET inhibition with OTX015/MK-8628 in four patients with advanced NUT midline carcinoma, with confirmed BRD4-NUT fusions, found early clinical benefits reported for two patients with one achieving post-treatment disease stabilization (Stathis et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to a clinical study by Stathis et al., 2016.

claim: In 2011, Dawson et al. demonstrated targeting BET proteins as an effective strategy for modulating aberrant gene expression associated with mixed-lineage leukaemia (MLL).
source: In 2011, Dawson et al. demonstrated targeting BET proteins as an effective strategy for modulating aberrant gene expression associated with mixed-lineage leukaemia (MLL), a genetically distinct form of acute leukaemia.
evidence: Supported by citation to the original study by Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: Selective inhibition of cell viability and BCL2 expression in leukaemia cells harboring MLL fusions was observed with the BET bromodomain inhibitor, I-BET151, in contrast to leukaemia cells with alternate oncogenic drivers.
source: Selective inhibition of cell viability and BCL2 expression in leukaemia cells harboring MLL fusions was observed with the BET bromodomain inhibitor, I-BET151, in contrast to leukaemia cells with alternate oncogenic drivers (Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to the original study by Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: Efficacy of I-BET151 was tested in a xenograft model of MLL, which resulted in a statistically significant increase in survival compared to vehicle control treated animals in the original study.
source: Furthermore, efficacy of I-BET151 was tested in a xenograft model of MLL, which resulted in a statistically significant increase in survival compared to vehicle control treated animals.
evidence: Supported by reference to the original study's findings.

claim: BCL2 is a key antiapoptotic gene that has been implicated in MLL-fusion leukaemias.
source: A key antiapoptotic gene, BCL2, which has been implicated in MLL-fusion leukaemias (Robinson et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2011), was reported in Dawson et al. (2011) to be selectively inhibited by I-BET151, suggesting a possible mode of action.
evidence: Supported by citations to studies by Robinson et al., 2008 and Wang et al., 2011.

claim: The xenograft mouse model imitates the pathology of human leukaemia by disseminating to the bone marrow.
source: Prior to conducting this efficacy experiment, we determined the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of I-BET151 in this xenograft mouse model, which imitates the pathology of human leukaemia by disseminating to the bone marrow (Lopes de Menezes et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to a study by Lopes de Menezes et al., 2005.

claim: NOD-SCID mice have a high rate of spontaneous thymic lymphomas.
source: While it has been previously noted that NOD-SCID mice have a high rate of spontaneous thymic lymphomas, no other tumor types were previously reported and tumors did not manifest until 20 weeks of age (Prochazka et al., 1992).
evidence: Supported by citation to a study by Prochazka et al., 1992.

claim: The method of conditioning can influence overall and hematological toxicity, as well as overall survival, despite similar engraftment levels.
source: The regimen used in this replication attempt has not been fully evaluated with MV4;11 cells regarding its impact on disease progression and treatment responsiveness, an important consideration, since the method of conditioning can influence overall and hematological toxicity, as well as overall survival, despite similar engraftment levels (Robert-Richard et al., 2006; Saland et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to studies by Robert-Richard et al., 2006 and Saland et al., 2015.
